title: Reference vs Pointer
concept: A reference is a safe alias that cannot be null and cannot be rebound.

steps.title: Create variables a and b
steps.explanation: Two int variables are allocated on the stack.

steps.title: Create a reference ref
steps.explanation: `ref` is an alias for `a`. They share the same address, and once bound, they cannot be changed to other variables.

steps.title: Create pointer ptr
steps.explanation: `ptr` is a separate variable that stores the address of `a`. Unlike references, they occupy their own memory.

steps.title: Pointer reallocation
steps.explanation: With `ptr = &b` a pointer can point to another variable. On the other hand, `ref` still points only to `a`.

steps.title: Check results
steps.explanation:
`ref` still outputs `a` (10) and `*ptr` outputs `b` (20).

**Key difference**: Pointers can be reassigned, references cannot.

quiz.question: What is the difference between a reference and a pointer?
options: References must be initialized when declared
References can also be rebound to other variables later.
A pointer has its own memory address
quiz.explanation: Once a reference is bound, it points to the same object until the end. Rebinding is not possible.

misconceptions.wrong: References can be reassigned to other variables
misconceptions.correct: ref = b copies the value of b to a pointed to by ref, not changing the target of ref.
misconceptions.why: A reference is an alias, so all operations on ref apply to the original variable.

keyTakeaway: A pointer is a variable that holds an address, and a reference is another name for the original. Choose according to your purpose.
